title: Grateful Dead Live at The Spectrum on 1973-09-21
taper: Thanks to Dr. Bruce Fried for lending me his dat.

ai_review.summary: Matrix recording praised for its clean balance captures a strong 1973 show highlighted by a perfect Black Peter and tight Jack Straw, though a few edits leave Sing Your Blues cut and Let It Grow a bit mushy.
ai_review.review: The performance is generally regarded as a solid mid‑’73 set with standout moments like Black Peter, Jack Straw and an inspired Weather Report Suite jam. The matrix source offers clear, balanced audio, but one reviewer notes a missing intro on Sing Your Blues and a dragged ending to Let It Grow, giving the recording a few minor blemishes.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise both the show and the matrix recording (≈70% positive), but one low‑rating review points out editing cuts and a mushy ending, pulling the overall assessment toward a mixed yet still strong rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clean and balanced mix; minor issues include an edited-out intro on Sing Your Blues and a slightly mushy tail on Let It Grow according to one reviewer.

standout_songs: Weather Report Suite (Let It Grow jam)
He's Gone > Truckin' > Drums & Bass > The Other One
poor_songs: Let It Grow (dragged out / mushy ending)
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set follows a standard early‑’73 list with the surprise addition of Black Peter; horns from Doug Sahm’s band join after a brief mic setup delay, adding color. The second set is a long medley featuring He's Gone into Truckin', an extended drum & bass segment leading into The Other One, then Wharf Rat and Row Jimmy, keeping the energy high throughout.
